diffs.diff: header pin 5: part says RXD, datasheet reading says RX
diffs.evidence: Winsen MH-Z19B manual v1.6, 'Terminal connection type' table: 'Pin 5  UART(RXD)TTL Level data input'. The pin-version table names the same signal 'Rx  UART(RXD)TTL Level data input' (v1.7 identical), so RX and RXD are the same sensor-input pin; the part's RXD (sensor data in, wire to MCU TX) matches. Manual also: 'Connect module's Vin-GND-RXD-TXD to users' 5V-GND-TXD-RXD.'

diffs.diff: header pin 6: part says TXD, datasheet reading says TX
diffs.evidence: Winsen MH-Z19B manual v1.6, 'Terminal connection type' table: 'Pin 6  UART(TXD)TTL Level data output'. The pin-version table names it 'Tx  UART(TXD)TTL Level data output' (v1.7 identical), so TX and TXD are the same sensor-output pin; the part's TXD (sensor data out, wire to MCU RX) matches.

diffs.diff: co2_ppm: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Winsen MH-Z19B manual v1.6, command 0x86 reply 'FF 86 HIGH LOW - - - - Checksum', 'CO2 concentration = HIGH * 256 + LOW' (example 01 F4 -> 500 ppm), i.e. 1 ppm per count. The part models exactly this: sim.uartReplies 16-bit 'value' field with scale 1, and the driver returns buf[2]*256+buf[3]. The gate reported 'none' only because its conversion extractor reads sim.responses/measure, not sim.uartReplies.
